summary: Feed s144_double is degraded: 2 high-severity faults. 8.5% of frames exceed IDS 1518-byte MTU and are dropped by NIC, plus microbursts to 2.78 Gbps overload the 1 Gbps IDS port (278% capacity). IDS is missing significant traffic and detection coverage is compromised.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo frames (up to 8058 bytes) from the monitored network without MTU normalization. The IDS tool port is standard 1518-byte MTU and its NIC silently drops oversized frames.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS never sees 163/1908 frames (8.5%). Any attack, exploit or C2 hidden in large frames is invisible, flow reassembly fails, and IDS signatures cannot fire on dropped traffic.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs_full_payload=true so slicing would break detection. Enable 9000-byte jumbo MTU on IDS NIC/port and packet broker egress, or configure broker to fragment/normalize jumbo frames to <=1518 bytes before delivery.

findings.root_cause: Aggregated traffic delivered to a single 1 Gbps IDS port bursts to 2.78 Gbps in 1ms intervals. No load-balancing or rate-shaping on the packet broker, so microbursts exceed line-rate capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and randomly drops packets during 9 overloaded intervals. IDS loses both directions of flows intermittently, misses exploits, creates false negatives and breaks stateful detection.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3+ IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization <80% and preserve flow symmetry (IDS needs_both_directions=true) while absorbing 2.78 Gbps bursts.
